HEADLINE: Serbia votes as students seek to unseat Aleksandar Vucic in snap election

SOURCED TIMES — THIS IS THE ONLY APPROVED SOURCE I FOUND CARRYING THEM
- Polling stations opened at 7 a.m. local time. Serbia is on CET (UTC+1) after the EU clock change of 25 Oct, so 7 a.m. local = 06:00 GMT.
- "Voting ends at 8 p.m. with first indications of results expected around two hours later." 8 p.m. CET = 19:00 GMT. First indications therefore around 22:00 CET = 21:00 GMT.
- "Unusually long lines formed at polling stations in Belgrade and Novi Sad before the start of voting at 7 a.m."

NOT CARRIED BY THIS SOURCE
- No turnout figure of any kind.
- No registered-voter total.
- No number of parliamentary seats contested.

CONTEXT
- The vote is a test of whether Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) can extend its 14-year grip on power and stave off a student-led movement born of recent protests.
- Ipsos poll published Thursday: SNS 47 percent, Student List 40 percent. Other polls have put the students ahead.
- The Student List fields a roster of 250 largely unfamiliar candidates, led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic.

CROSS-REFERENCE: Al Jazeera, "Serbia votes in election pitting longtime leader against student movement", published 25 Oct 2026 (cache file MORN-GEO-AlJazeera-serbia-votes.txt), carries the same Ipsos 47/40 figures, the Srdanovic leadership and the 250-candidate roster, and the 150,000 Belgrade rally on Thursday, but carries NO poll opening or closing times and NO turnout.

NOTHING IS KNOWN ABOUT THE OUTCOME. At the 09:15 GMT publication slot, Serbian polls will have been open for roughly three and a quarter hours and no result, exit poll or turnout figure will exist.
